actual_current_destination_openings.first_line: - **The EUR 800 GWG test** uses cost reduced by the input VAT contained in the price (§ 6(2) EStG: "vermindert um einen darin enthaltenen Vorsteuerbetrag"), including where it is not recoverable. Keep eligibility separate from the deductible expense: [§ 9b(1) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__9b.html) excludes recoverable VAT from acquisition cost; irrecoverable VAT remains in cost. An otherwise eligible self-usable business chair at EUR 952 gross (EUR 800 plus 19% VAT, [§ 12(1) UStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ustg_1980/__12.html)) meets the EUR 800 test in both cases. A Kleinunternehmer can choose to expense the full EUR 952; a business entitled to full input-VAT credit expenses EUR 800 and claims the EUR 152 VAT separately.

Test the EUR 200,000 profit limit without both investment deductions and § 7g(2) add-backs; a tested profit of EUR 200,001 fails for that year; the EUR 200,000 cap on open deductions is a different rule with the same number. A deduction may create a loss. Not bought by the end of the third year after: it is undone in the year taken (§ 7g(3)). In the year bought, up to the same share of the real cost is added back (not more than the open deductions) and the cost may be cut by as much (§ 7g(2)). The asset must be let or used only or almost only (at least 90%) in a German establishment until the end of the year after purchase (§ 7g(4)). Special depreciation of up to 40% also needs the profit limit met in the year before purchase (§ 7g(5), (6)).

actual_current_destination_openings.first_line: - **Prepayments (§ 37 EStG).** Due 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December (§ 37(1)); both minimums must be met. Set by notice, as a rule from the last assessment's tax less tax withheld. components.exact_old_line: 3. **Trader with the § 35 credit** ([§ 35 EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__35.html)). Trade profit EUR 110,000, the only income; taxable income EUR 100,000; assumed trade tax multiplier (Hebesatz) 400%. Tariff tax 0.42 x 100,000 - 11,135.63 = 30,864.37, so EUR 30,864. Trade tax base amount (110,000 - 24,500) x 3.5% = EUR 2,992.50 ([§ 11 GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__11.html)); trade tax at 400% = EUR 11,970 (details in `de-trade-tax`). Credit 4 x 2,992.50 = EUR 11,970, within both caps. Income tax EUR 18,894: below EUR 20,350, so no surcharge. Church tax (9%) is on EUR 30,864, not on EUR 18,894: EUR 2,777.76 ([§ 51a(2) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__51a.html)).

actual_current_destination_openings.first_line: **Example 3: sole trader with the § 35 credit, Hebesatz 400%.** A single online retailer (trade, § 15 EStG). Trade profit EUR 110,000, his only income; special expenses EUR 10,000, so taxable income EUR 100,000, zone 4. Tariff tax 0.42 x 100,000 - 11,135.63 = 30,864.37, so EUR 30,864. Trade tax: trade income EUR 110,000 (already a multiple of EUR 100) less the EUR 24,500 allowance = EUR 85,500; base amount 85,500 x 3.5% = EUR 2,992.50 ([§ 11 GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__11.html)); at a 400% Hebesatz the municipality charges EUR 11,970. Credit: 4 x 2,992.50 = EUR 11,970. First cap: all his income is trade income, so the share of tariff tax on it is the full EUR 30,864. Second cap: trade tax payable EUR 11,970. The credit is EUR 11,970 ([§ 35(1) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__35.html)). Income tax EUR 18,894, below EUR 20,350, so no surcharge. Church tax at 9% is worked out on the tax before the § 35 credit ([§ 51a(2) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__51a.html)): 9% x 30,864 = EUR 2,777.76. Total income tax plus trade tax EUR 30,864: at a 400% Hebesatz 4 x the base amount equals the trade tax, so the credit absorbs it in full; above 400% the credit stops at 4 x the base amount and the rest of the trade tax is a real cost.

actual_current_destination_openings.first_line: - **May or must.** The surcharge may be set for any late return unless the delay is excusable (§ 152(1)). It is compulsory after 14 months (or when a return called in early misses its date, § 152(2) no. 3), unless the deadline was extended, the tax is nil or below, or the tax is not above prepayments plus tax withheld (§ 152(3)); it then stays possible at discretion.
actual_current_destination_openings.last_line: - **Example.** A 2026 return without an adviser filed three months and five days after Monday 2 August 2027, balance EUR 2,000: 0.25% x 2,000 = EUR 5 a month, below the EUR 25 minimum, so 4 started months x EUR 25 = EUR 100, if the office sets one.
